title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A mix of big-picture and feel-good news today. In Washington, Rep. Thomas Massie filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and the Supreme Court let border construction continue near Big Bend National Park. Closer to home for Charlotte, the city approved a big airport expansion. There's also some fun: a Jamaican teen hurdler set a Youth Olympic record and a Spanish freestyle rapper won 197 battles in a single day.

stories.headline: Rep. Massie files impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth
stories.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, the first day the House was back after the midterms. Most of the charges relate to the war with Iran and whether it followed the War Powers Resolution. Other charges cover strikes on alleged drug boats, the capture of Venezuela's president without congressional approval, and actions related to Sen. Mark Kelly. President Trump and Hegseth both rejected the effort, and a House vote could come within days.
key_facts: The resolution lists 8 charges, including 3 tied to the Iran war under the War Powers Resolution.
Massie tried this in September, but Speaker Mike Johnson called an early recess, so the resolution expired.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said he is a "hard yes"; Trump said "I'll stand by him."
Massie lost his May primary to Trump-endorsed challenger Ed Gallrein.
stories.why: At its core, this is a test of how war powers are split between Congress and the president, and it could be the first impeachment of a Cabinet secretary in Trump's second term.

stories.headline: Recycling plant workers treated after white powder exposure in Lenoir
stories.summary: On Monday, workers at Prime Recycling in Lenoir, North Carolina, opened packages that had a white powder on them, and the powder got into the air. Twenty-two people felt ill, mostly with breathing trouble and burning eyes, and about 14 were taken to the hospital. Officials say the patients are in stable condition. Hazmat teams are still working to identify the substance.
key_facts: 22 people were assessed at the scene, and 14 were taken to UNC Caldwell.
Officials said the patients are stable and the injuries are non-life-threatening.
The State Bureau of Investigation and the Asheville Fire hazmat team responded.
disputed: The substance and how it got into the facility are still unknown.
Reports differ on how many were hospitalized: one outlet says 11, others say 14.
stories.why: Everyone is reported stable, and investigators are working to find out what the powder was.

stories.headline: Charlotte approves $2.1 billion airport expansion deal
stories.summary: Charlotte City Council approved a new 10.5-year airline lease at Charlotte Douglas International Airport, which clears the way for about $2.1 billion in projects. Plans include a bigger Concourse C, a passenger tunnel and a renovated international pavilion. Critics, including a consumer group and the SEIU union, wanted a delay over concerns about fares, competition and subcontractor working conditions. Supporters call the airport the city's economic engine.
key_facts: American Airlines' gates will grow from 93 to 109.
Airlines' share of airport revenue will rise to 40-45%.
The airport estimates a $40 billion annual economic impact and 184,000 jobs in the Carolinas.
More than 50 people signed up to speak at public comment, many of them against the deal.
stories.why: If you fly out of Charlotte, this probably means more direct flights and more construction over the next decade. Some worry it could also mean higher fares.

stories.headline: Jamaica's Marquies Page wins hurdles gold in Dakar
stories.summary: Jamaican teen Marquies Page won the boys' 110m hurdles at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, finishing well ahead of the field in 12.95 seconds. Jamaica also picked up silver medals in the shot put and discus.
key_facts: Page won in 12.95 seconds.
China's Shijie Chen took silver (13.40) and South Africa's Enrique Bosch took bronze (13.45).
Xhaevion Kelly won silver in the shot put and Kamari Kennedy won silver in the discus.
stories.why: It was a great day for young Jamaican athletes.

stories.headline: Cardi B and Jamaican festival organizers argue over a canceled show
stories.summary: The organizers of Jamaica's BZR WKND festival say they plan to sue Cardi B after she skipped her October headline slot and a rescheduled December date. Cardi B says she was only paid half her fee and is threatening to countersue. Ticket holders are being refunded.
key_facts: CEO Ryan Burke says Cardi B was paid US$2.5 million in full.
Cardi B says on Instagram Live that she received only a US$1 million deposit.
The show was set for October 16-18, with a makeup date of December 20.
disputed: The amount paid is disputed: the organizers say $2.5M, while Cardi B says a $1M deposit.
Both sides have only threatened legal action; there is no report of a lawsuit being filed yet.
stories.why: If you bought a ticket, organizers say refunds are underway.

links.title: Cardi B threatens legal action against BZR WKND organisers

stories.headline: Page sets a Youth Olympic record, beating a 12-year-old mark
stories.summary: Sixteen-year-old Marquies Page won Jamaica's first gold of the Youth Olympic Games with a 12.95 in the 110m hurdles. That broke the Youth Olympic record of 12.96, set by fellow Jamaican Jaheel Hyde in 2014. It was also a big personal best for Page, beating his previous 13.06.
key_facts: Page's time of 12.95 seconds beat Jaheel Hyde's 2014 record of 12.96.
Page is 16 and runs for St Jago High.
He was a semi-finalist at the World Under-20 Championships in August.
stories.why: A Jamaican teen broke a record held by another Jamaican.

stories.headline: Tied at the top before the Jamaica Golf Open's final round
stories.summary: Nicholas Estrada of the USA and Justin Hastings of the Cayman Islands are tied at nine under par going into Tuesday's final round of the 58th Jamaica Golf Open at Tryall Club. Wind and tricky pin placements made Monday tougher. Mac McClair had the round of the day for drama, with back-to-back eagles followed later by back-to-back bogeys.
key_facts: The leaders are both at 9 under (135).
Canadian Ty Celone and Tyler Stachkunas are tied for third at 3 under.
Jamaica's Justin Burrowes is in eighth at 1 under.
Estrada is mentored by 1958 champion Bob Toski, who recently turned 100.
stories.why: It's a two-man tie going into a final-day showdown.

stories.headline: Supreme Court lets Big Bend border construction go ahead for now
stories.summary: The Supreme Court lifted a lower court's pause, so border barrier construction can continue in and around Big Bend National Park in Texas while the lawsuit plays out. The unsigned decision said the federal judge lacked authority to block the work and noted that federal law lets DHS waive environmental rules. The project has drawn objections from people across the political spectrum who worry about the park's landscape, wildlife and tourism.
key_facts: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only dissent.
The plans include 30-foot steel barriers, patrol roads and surveillance systems.
The lawsuit was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, a local historic-church nonprofit and a landowner.
stories.why: This decides what happens to a well-loved national park while the larger court case continues.
